articles.title: Your Brain Starts Changing Within Two Minutes of Meditation. By Seven Minutes, It Peaks.
articles.excerpt: A study from India's NIMHANS, using the Isha Yoga breath-watching tradition, shows measurable neural shifts happen faster than anyone assumed. For time-starved diaspora professionals, the science says even brief practice works.
articles.image_caption: A person practicing breath-focused meditation outdoors at sunset
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Single Gut Procedure Just Preserved 78 Per Cent of GLP-1 Weight Loss at One Year. South Asians Should Watch This Closely.
articles.excerpt: Fractyl Health's REVEAL-1 data show that its endoscopic Revita procedure helps patients maintain weight after stopping Wegovy or Mounjaro — without lifelong medication. For a community with the world's highest metabolic disease burden, the implications are significant.
articles.image_caption: An endoscopic procedure being performed in a clinical setting
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Keto Diet Just Put 72 Per Cent of Anorexia Patients Into Recovery. The Science Is Counterintuitive and Compelling.
articles.excerpt: A UC San Diego pilot trial published in Nature's Communications Medicine found that 14 weeks of supervised ketogenic therapy reversed eating-disorder symptoms in nearly three out of four participants — without triggering weight loss.
articles.image_caption: A spread of ketogenic-friendly foods rich in healthy fats, including avocado, nuts and seeds
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Scientists Built a Factory for Gut Bacteria. It Could Replace the Most Unpleasant Treatment in Medicine.
articles.excerpt: A Mount Sinai team has developed a manufacturing platform for targeted mixtures of beneficial gut bacteria, offering a standardised alternative to faecal transplants. For South Asians with elevated antibiotic use, the implications are personal.
articles.image_caption: A laboratory setting where scientists study gut microbiome composition
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Swapping 30 Minutes of Sitting for a Brisk Walk Cuts Depression by 9 Per Cent. For Desk-Bound NRIs, the Maths Is Simple.
articles.excerpt: A new study in Depression and Anxiety finds that exercise intensity, not just movement, is the key to mental health at midlife. South Asians in sedentary tech jobs should take note.
articles.image_caption: A person walking briskly outdoors for exercise
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Daily Coffee Is Rewiring Your Gut and Your Brain. A New Study Explains How.
articles.excerpt: Researchers found that coffee reshapes the gut microbiome, alters neurotransmitter levels, and changes behaviour — and caffeine is not the only driver.
articles.image_caption: A cup of freshly brewed coffee — the drink reshaping gut microbiomes worldwide
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air Pollution Is Erasing Your Brain's Encyclopedia Faster Than Ageing Itself. South Asians Should Be Alarmed.
articles.excerpt: A 17-year study found that breathing polluted air degrades the memory system you use for language, facts, and everyday comprehension — and the damage exceeds a decade of normal cognitive decline.
articles.image_caption: Smog blankets a city skyline as fine particulate matter fills the air
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ultra-Processed Foods Raise Dementia Risk by 58 Per Cent. South Asians in the West Are Eating More of Them Than Ever.
articles.excerpt: A Harvard-led study of 5,000 older Americans finds processed meats are the biggest driver. The findings land as the Indian diaspora shifts further from traditional diets.
articles.image_caption: Packaged ultra-processed foods on grocery store shelves in the United States
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One Extra Slice of Deli Meat a Day Raises Stomach Cancer Risk by 9 Per Cent. The Diaspora Diet Is Drifting in the Wrong Direction.
articles.excerpt: A 14-year European study of 450,000 people links processed meat to stomach and oesophageal cancers. For NRI families eating more Western food, the data carries a specific warning.
articles.image_caption: Assorted processed meats including deli ham, sausages, and bacon at a market counter
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Cheap Supplement Just Made Diabetic Hearts 15 Per Cent More Efficient. South Asians Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: University of Leeds researchers found that mitoquinone reversed early signs of heart damage in Type 2 diabetes patients within four months. A larger trial is next.
articles.image_caption: Mitochondria are the energy factories inside heart cells that diabetes progressively damages
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A 30-Year Harvard Study Found the Exact Amount of Strength Training That Lowers Death Risk. It Is Less Than You Think.
articles.excerpt: Ninety to 120 minutes per week cut cardiovascular mortality by 19 per cent and neurological death by 27 per cent. Beyond that, the returns flatlined.
articles.image_caption: A woman performing strength training exercises with dumbbells
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Turmeric Is 2026's Herb of the Year. But the Science Behind Curcumin May Not Be What You Think.
articles.excerpt: The West spent $275 million studying curcumin. Indian families have been drinking haldi doodh for centuries. A new review asks who was right.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Immunotherapy Drug Just Kept 85 Per Cent of Bladder Cancer Patients Tumour-Free Without Surgery. It Could Change Everything.
articles.excerpt: A trial at the Institute of Cancer Research shows durvalumab combined with chemoradiation may spare thousands from life-altering bladder removal surgery.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Your Baby's Gut Microbiome Starts Diverging by Six Months if Allergies Are Coming. South Asian Families Should Take Note.
articles.excerpt: A new study in Frontiers in Microbiomes found that infants who develop eczema or food allergies show distinct gut microbiome differences by mid-infancy — and South Asian children are among the most affected populations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: If You Feel Older Than You Are, It Is Probably Ruining Your Sleep. A New Study Explains Why.
articles.excerpt: A study of 3,177 adults found that people who feel older than their chronological age sleep worse, feel worse during the day, and report poorer physical health — a pattern that may hit the overworked Indian diaspora especially hard.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Scientists Built Living Microrobots That Repaired Spinal Cord Injuries in Mice. India Has One of the Highest Rates of Such Injuries in the World.
articles.excerpt: A team at ETH Zurich combined stem cells with magnetoelectric nanoparticles to create tiny machines that can be guided to injury sites and stimulate nerve regrowth. The study, published in Nature Materials, restored movement in paralysed mice within weeks.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Four-Week Yoga Programme Just Showed It Can Sharply Reduce Insomnia and Anxiety in Cancer Survivors. The Practice Was Born in India.
articles.excerpt: A large randomised trial presented at the 2026 ASCO meeting found that yoga significantly reduced fatigue, mood disturbance, and sleep problems after cancer treatment. For the diaspora community, the findings are both validation and vindication.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Daily Pill Just Doubled Survival for Pancreatic Cancer. For Diabetes-Prone South Asians, the Breakthrough Hits Close to Home.
articles.excerpt: Daraxonrasib, the first RAS inhibitor, cut the risk of death by 60 per cent in a 500-patient trial — the largest gain ever recorded for advanced pancreatic cancer.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians have 2-3x higher pancreatic cancer risk due to genetic predisposition to Type 2 diabetes. Dr. Shubham Pant, an Indian-origin oncologist at MD Anderson, co-led the trial.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cigna Just Dropped GLP-1 Weight Loss Coverage for Its Own Employees. If You Are South Asian and on Wegovy, Read This.
articles.excerpt: The insurer will stop covering Wegovy and Zepbound for weight loss on July 1. Other employers may follow — and the diaspora has the most to lose.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians develop metabolic disease at lower BMI thresholds. Many tech professionals carry Cigna plans. Losing GLP-1 coverage forces a choice between cash-pay and medication discontinuation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Scientists Calculated the Exact Sleep Window That Slows Ageing. It Is Not Eight Hours.
articles.excerpt: A study of half a million people published in Nature found that sleeping between 6.4 and 7.8 hours a night produced the youngest biological age across nearly every organ. For South Asians who sleep too little or too much, the findings are a wake-up call.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Weight-Loss Drugs Just Showed They May Cut Cancer Risk by Up to 71 Per Cent. South Asians Should Be Paying Close Attention.
articles.excerpt: Six studies presented at ASCO 2026 found GLP-1 medications linked to dramatically lower rates of pancreatic, lung, breast, and blood cancers. The implications for a community with among the world's highest diabetes rates are enormous.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Compound in Strawberries Just Showed It Can Reduce the Brain Proteins Behind Alzheimer's. The Catch Is in Your Genes.
articles.excerpt: Brain autopsies from 575 people in the Rush Memory and Aging Project found that high pelargonidin intake from berries was linked to fewer amyloid plaques and tau tangles — but only in people without the APOE ε4 risk gene.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Two-Year Calorie Restriction Trial Just Revealed Why You Age Faster Than You Should. The Answer Is in Your Immune System.
articles.excerpt: A landmark Nature Aging study found that cutting 14 per cent of daily calories deactivated complement proteins that drive chronic inflammation — the same proteins that run high in South Asians decades before heart disease strikes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Personalised mRNA Vaccine Just Halved Melanoma Recurrence Over Five Years. Cancer Treatment May Never Be the Same.
articles.excerpt: Moderna and Merck's KEYNOTE-942 trial shows the vaccine kept 92 per cent of patients alive at the five-year mark, compared with 71 per cent on standard immunotherapy alone. South Asians, often diagnosed later, have the most to gain from a treatment that learns each tumour's fingerprint.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Harvard Study Found the Best Diet for Weight Management During Menopause. Indian Kitchens Already Follow Most of It.
articles.excerpt: A 38,000-woman study in JAMA Network Open found that a planetary health diet cut obesity risk by 54 per cent during menopause. Dal, whole wheat roti, nuts, and mustard oil — staples of Indian cooking — are at the core of what researchers recommend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Night Owls Are Not Just Tired. A New Study Says They Are Lonelier, and It Is Making Them Anxious.
articles.excerpt: Research presented at SLEEP 2026 finds that nocturnal loneliness is the key pathway linking late sleep patterns to higher anxiety — a finding that hits close to home for South Asians staying up to call family across time zones.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Insomnia Triples Breast Cancer Risk in Women Under 50. A New Study Just Made Sleep a Cancer Conversation.
articles.excerpt: Research presented at ASCO 2026 found that women diagnosed with insomnia were three times more likely to develop breast cancer within five years. For South Asian women — who face unique sleep pressures — the findings demand attention.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Mediterranean Diet May Lower Anxiety in Teenagers. South Asian Families Already Have Half the Ingredients.
articles.excerpt: A new study in Nutrients found that teens who eat a Mediterranean-style diet report fewer anxiety symptoms. For Indian families, the overlap with traditional home cooking is striking — and the gaps are fixable.
articles.nri_angle: Traditional South Asian cooking already overlaps significantly with the Mediterranean diet — legumes, whole grains, spices. The gaps (fatty fish, olive oil, berries) are specific and actionable for Indian families raising teens in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Walking Is Not Enough. A New Study Says Vigorous Exercise and Sleep Are What Actually Protect Your Mental Health.
articles.excerpt: A University of Oulu study of middle-aged adults found that moderate-to-vigorous physical activity and adequate sleep dramatically reduced symptoms of depression and anxiety — and light walking barely moved the needle.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians in the US are among the least physically active ethnic groups, with lower rates of vigorous exercise. The community favors light walking over intense activity, but this study shows intensity matters more than duration for mental health protection.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Is Rediscovering Whole Grain Flour. Indian Families Have Been Grinding Their Own Atta for Generations.
articles.excerpt: The craft flour movement sweeping Brooklyn bakeries and MAHA influencer feeds has a familiar parallel in every Indian kitchen that still uses a chakki.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bovine Colostrum Is the Latest Gut Health Obsession. Your Grandmother Called It Kharvas and Ate It Decades Ago.
articles.excerpt: TikTok influencers are spending $50 a tub on what Indian families have been eating for generations. The science is finally catching up — but it is more complicated than the wellness industry wants you to believe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mosquitoes Can Learn to Love the Smell of DEET. If You Are Visiting India This Summer, Read This.
articles.excerpt: A new study in the Journal of Experimental Biology found that after just three exposures, 60 per cent of mosquitoes tried to bite the hand covered in repellent. For NRIs heading into monsoon season, the timing could not be worse.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The American Heart Association Just Said Exercise Protects Your Heart Even if You Never Lose Weight. South Asians Need to Hear This.
articles.excerpt: A landmark scientific statement in Circulation says physical activity reduces cardiovascular risk independent of the scale. For a community with the highest heart disease rates in the country, the implications are urgent.

sources.label: AHA 2026 Heart Disease and Stroke Statistics

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Four Adults With a 'Normal' BMI Are Actually Obese. For South Asians, the Numbers Are Worse.
articles.excerpt: A USC study of 5,642 Americans found that BMI misses dangerous hidden fat. For a community that develops diabetes and heart disease at lower body weights, this is a wake-up call.

sources.label: WHO Expert Consultation on BMI in Asian Populations (2004)

articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Medicare Will Cover Wegovy and Zepbound for $50 a Month Starting July 1. If Your Parents Are on Medicare, Read This.
articles.excerpt: The new GLP-1 Bridge program opens weight-loss drug access to 14 million Medicare beneficiaries. For NRI families managing ageing parents' health from abroad, the financial and logistical implications are substantial.
articles.nri_angle: Many NRI families have elderly parents on Medicare. South Asians face higher visceral fat accumulation and metabolic syndrome at lower BMIs. The $50 GLP-1 programme directly impacts diaspora families managing elder care remotely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
